A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EnvGS and contain readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material. Content can be matched across appendix moves and renumbering without material evidence gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments, rendering-speed measurements, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical evaluations and reports additional masked-region comparisons, baseline results, and a perceptual-loss ablation.

M1.justification: The two Gaussian representations, rendering procedure, joint optimization, and training losses remain unchanged. Newly stated SH and pruning settings provide implementation documentation without establishing a procedural revision.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Ref-Real, NeRF-Casting Shiny Scenes, Shiny Blender, Mip-NeRF 360, and the self-captured Audi and Dog scenes. V2's masked-region evaluation uses existing images and changes evaluation procedures rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated ENVIDR and NDE comparisons on Ref-Real and NeRF-Casting scenes in Table 5 and Figure 7. The existing benchmark comparator sets remain intact; ENVIDR was previously cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: V2 introduces reflective-foreground and near-field evaluation masks, with metrics computed after compositing masked regions onto white backgrounds (Appendix A.1). The existing splits, image resolutions, and full-image evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds a perceptual-loss removal ablation in Table 4 and targeted reflection-region analysis in Table 2 and Figure 6. The separate-versus-shared Gaussian experiment is retained, moving from Section 5.4 to Appendix B.3; existing environment-map and speed analyses also remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial result groups for masked regions, ENVIDR/NDE comparisons, and training times. Audi scores change for every method: EnvGS PSNR changes from 27.604 to 28.629, while Ref-NeRF changes from 27.078 to 24.529, moving from second to last. Full-model ablation and runtime values also change. Original per-scene benchmark tables remain numerically identical. The cause of the Audi revisions is unspecified.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and gradient derivations are retained. V1's Equations 2–3 are combined into v2's Equation 2, and the gradient appendix moves from C to D; these are presentation changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about environment Gaussians, differentiable real-time tracing, and high-quality near-field and high-frequency reflections. Additional experiments support the existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new ablation as showing that perceptual loss provides only marginal benefits, and discusses object-level methods struggling with real scenes containing backgrounds. The transparent/refractive-material limitation and explanation of shared-Gaussian optimization failure are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix C documents an SH setting of 2, approximately 300,000 environment Gaussians using 70 MB, and pruning to at most 630,000 primitives by rendering weight. V2 also explains mask construction and reports training times, including 2.5 hours for EnvGS. These are additional disclosures.

R1.justification: V2 adds nine references, including NDE, concurrent Ref-GS, and seven broader vision/graphics references. Section 2 briefly distinguishes Ref-GS's near-field and far-field representations, while the existing research positioning remains largely intact.

P1.justification: Existing prose receives limited editing. V2 adds appendix subsections, moves the separate-Gaussian discussion to Appendix B.3, and renumbers the gradient appendix. A corresponding-author footnote and acknowledgements are also added; the main narrative structure remains stable.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 2 and 5 and Figures 6 and 7, extends Table 1 with training times, and adds an ablation row. Table headers, highlighting, and placement are revised. Original figure imagery is retained, with supplementary figures relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The regional evaluations and perceptual-loss ablation provide more direct evidence for the reflection-specific contribution, while Appendix C improves reproducibility. These are useful, bounded gains. Unexplained Audi score revisions and changes to full-model ablation/runtime values limit confidence in the numerical updates.
